question.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{5}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{6{x}^{7}-3{x}^{3}-4}{2{x}^{5}+7} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{6{x}^{7}}{{x}^{5}}-\frac{3{x}^{3}}{{x}^{5}}-\frac{4}{{x}^{5}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{5}}{{x}^{5}}+\frac{7}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{(6{x}^{2}-\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{4}{{x}^{3}})}{(2+\frac{7}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{6{x}^{2}-0-0}{2+0} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }3{x}^{2} \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
